questions.q: What naming convention does this project use for intermediate models?
options: `raw_<entity>`
`int_<entity>__<verb>ed`, e.g. `int_orders__joined`
`fct_<entity>`
`stg_<entity>`
questions.explain: int_orders__joined follows the project's int_<entity>__<verb>ed convention for anything between staging and marts.

questions.q: What does `int_orders__joined.sql` use instead of `{{ source(...) }}`, and why?
options: Two `{{ ref(...) }}` calls, because it reads from other models (the customers mart and the orders staging model), not a raw source
A hard-coded table name, because ref() doesn't work across models
No reference function at all — it's plain SQL
`{{ source(...) }}` twice, same as a staging model
questions.explain: Reading from other models via ref() rather than a raw source is exactly what makes a model intermediate rather than staging.

questions.q: Why does the model use `left join` instead of `inner join` when joining orders to customers?
options: Because dbt doesn't support inner joins
To keep every order row even if a matching customer record is missing, instead of silently dropping orders
Because left join runs faster in every case
It doesn't matter which join type is used here
questions.explain: An inner join here would make orders silently disappear from downstream totals if a customer record were ever missing — left join avoids that silent data loss.

questions.q: What is deliberately NOT included in this intermediate model yet?
options: The customer_id column
Payments data and a revenue total
The order_id column
The order's status
questions.explain: This model's only job is orders joined to who placed them — payments join in starting Lesson 6.

questions.q: How can you confirm the join didn't accidentally drop rows?
options: There's no reliable way to confirm this
Check that the model compiles without a syntax error
Confirm `int_orders__joined`'s row count exactly matches `stg_jaffle_shop__orders`'s row count
Open the model in Power BI and eyeball the total
questions.explain: A lower row count than the orders staging model is the concrete tell that an inner join quietly dropped unmatched rows.
